_documentation: Hand-curated controlled vocabulary for the directory's research-interest keywords. Several sections drive the same surface. `acronyms` is a flat list of preferred display forms (UN, NATO, EU, IoT, …); when one of those words appears anywhere in a submitted keyword, the sync emits it in the canonical form rather than letting the sentence-case normaliser mangle it. `proper_nouns` works identically but for capitalised place names (countries and regions): the sentence-case normaliser only capitalises the first word of a keyword, so without this list a mid-phrase Afghanistan or Ukraine would render lowercased (`Russia-ukraine war`). Both lists are matched case-insensitively against each token and emitted in the exact form listed here, so keep each entry in its correct display form. `aliases` maps a canonical display form to a list of lowercased aliases that resolve to it; use this when two genuinely-distinct submitted phrases should collapse (e.g. `fpa` → `Foreign policy analysis`, or `political economy of europe` → `Political economy`). scripts/sync-bios.py reads this file, normalises each bio's `keywords` into a `canonical_keywords` field, and logs Levenshtein-close pairs that aren't already merged so the maintainer can decide whether to add them. A `spelling` section is a word-level map from American to British spellings (lowercased key → lowercased British form); during the word-walk each letter-run matching a key is rewritten to its British form before sentence-casing, so `Defense` becomes `Defence` and `Cyber defense` becomes `Cyber defence`. It deliberately omits `program`, which is valid British English in the computing sense. The file is hand-edited; changes land in the same PR that submits the new bio (or in a periodic curation pass).
